problem: Prior household rearrangement systems are mostly trained in simulation, restricted to single tasks or single rooms, ignore fine-grained manipulation, or depend on manually annotated prior semantic maps with exact receptacle locations; LLM-only approaches need heavy prompt engineering to capture user preferences.
motivation: A useful home robot must handle the full tidy-up loop: detect misplaced objects, decide user-specific placements, grasp unknown objects, and navigate across rooms to receptacles whose positions are not known in advance. Preferences are subjective, so generic common-sense reasoning is insufficient, and real-world deployment demands robustness to failures.
key_idea: A modular real-robot tidy-up pipeline that combines collaborative-filtering user preferences with open-vocabulary detection, learned grasping and heuristic semantic navigation, all orchestrated by behavior trees with retry logic.
insight: The paper is a systems integration demo; it offers no ablations. Its lesson is that a coarse 2D geometric map with room labels plus on-the-fly receptacle detection is sufficient for multi-room rearrangement, and behavior trees with retry decorators provide failure recovery (e.g., trying other candidate receptacles on place failure).
method: Semantic mapping and recognition: Cartographer builds a 2D LiDAR occupancy grid manually annotated with room labels; DETIC (20k classes) detects manipulable objects and receptacles, whose 3D positions are re-projected from depth into the map.

Object rearrangement: Housekeep human-labeled placement data forms a knowledge base for target rooms; collaborative filtering with matrix factorization (MSE + L2 loss) fills the sparse user-preference matrix to predict per-user room/receptacle ratings; an object is misplaced if its current location is not in the top-10 predicted locations.

Manipulation: Contact-GraspNet-style learned grasp prediction proposes grasp poses; the receptacle is added as a single collision entity and other objects as voxels; supports complex interactions such as opening a drawer via handle grasps and temporarily placing the held object.

Semantic navigation: Room-to-room navigation goes to the annotated room center with the Navfn planner; then the room is scanned for receptacles, the target receptacle is chosen from the preference module, and Carrot Planner approaches it.

Behavior-tree integration: BTs sequence misplaced-object detection, placement candidates, pickup, RoomNavigator, ReceptacleNavigator and PlaceBehavior; decorator nodes retry other candidate receptacles; blackboard passes messages; perception runs continuously; implemented on a Fetch robot in ROS.

setting.backbone: DETIC (pretrained detector), Contact-GraspNet-style grasp predictor, matrix-factorization collaborative filtering; heuristic Navfn/Carrot planners (no end-to-end policy)
setting.training_data: Pretrained DETIC (20k classes); Housekeep human-labeled placement preference dataset for the preference model; pretrained grasp network
setting.action_space: 2D navigation goals via Navfn/Carrot planners; arm motion planning with grasp poses
setting.privileged: manually annotated room labels on the 2D map (receptacle locations not given)

numbers_note: No quantitative results; experiments are qualitative real-world demonstrations (long-horizon mug/mustard bottle transfer, user-preference placement for two sampled users, Rubik's cube into drawer).
results: Qualitatively demonstrates a Fetch robot completing multi-room, multi-object tidy-up in a lab-built apartment (office, living room, kitchen), placing objects per sampled user preferences and handling a closed drawer. No success rates or baselines are reported.
limitations: Purely qualitative demonstrations in a single simple apartment; no quantitative metrics, baselines or ablations
Room labels are manually annotated and navigation uses heuristic planners
Unrecoverable failures (dropped object, hardware fault) end the episode; not tested across multiple environments or optimized for speed
compares_to: Castro et al. BT-based room-to-room navigation
